metadata.title: How Trump Accounts can turn $2K into $40K: Robinhood CEO & BNY CEO discuss

content.text:
Trump Accounts, the government-sponsored savings accounts for children, have officially launched.
Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) CEO Robin Vince and Robinhood (HOOD) CEO Vlad Tenev sit down with Yahoo Finance Senior Reporter Jennifer Schonberger to discuss the philosophy and benefits of the Trump Accounts program.
Go to TrumpAccounts.gov or download the Trump Accounts mobile app to get your child's account started.
The Treasury wanted to make these accounts the lowest cost possible to the American public. And they picked the lowest cost index funds, and this is free and a commission free account, right?
Yeah, that's right. So, I mean, one of the things that Robinhood became famous for was eliminating commissions. So it used to be that if you were an individual uh that wanted to buy a stock or an ETF, you would pay $7 to $10 every single transaction.
And there were account minimums. So you needed $1,000 or $2,000 uh to even get started. And now we came into the market and you look at this program, not only are there no account minimums, you can start with zero, but the Treasury is actually seeding $1,000 into the accounts.
So if you're a newborn, you get $1,000 seeded by the US Treasury to kickstart your investing journey.
And so, um, I think everyone should download the app, should tell everyone you know to download the app as well, uh because it's literally free money for newborns. Um,
And this is this this is a very important point, which is you've got to start early. Part of the part of the the process here is to get kids right at the very first day that they're born. so that all newborns can have a financial stake, as Vlad was saying, in the future of the country.
And by actually owning a piece of it, and the power of the compounding, the financial education, just think about it, $1,000, if every corporation in America matched that $1,000 with another thousand.
So you have $2,000. Over the course of 30 years, if we saw the same performance in the stock market that we've seen over the past 30 years, that would turn into $40,000. So 2,000 to 40. Now, imagine that same family put $10 a week additional into the account over the full period of time.
Now you'd have $140,000 over 30 years. That's a real stake. That's enough to be able to invest in a home and to be able to have a real additional element power to your American Dream.
And I'm glad you brought that up, Robin, because your company, your bank, BNY Melon, is pledging to match the $1,000 government contribution uh for your employees. Other companies have also signed up to pledge to do the same.
That's right. And we'd encourage more companies all around the US, big, small, to be able to find a way to do the same thing so that we can help turbo charge this uh early compounding uh investment in financial capitalism.
And what do you think this means in terms of the implications for the markets and the economy to have such a wave of new investors coming in?
Well, I think investor enthusiasm matters a lot. But so does a feeling for all Americans that they have a stake in our society because capitalism is our chosen approach to economic structure.
And to have 40% of Americans who today don't have a direct stake in that. They're not owners in the stock market. That's a problem. So increasing participation. So it's not only the kid's own financial future, but it's the parents, the guardians, everybody else who recognizes that being invested, being financially literate, and engaging and benefiting from this compounding is an incredibly valuable contribution to American society and the American Dream.
And just think about this stat, 86% of the Trump accounts that are actually open now are from households that earn less than $200,000.
So, it's a real democratization of access to investing. And that's a very important principle in the whole program.
